A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations, ColoredMNIST experiments, and ID/OOD correlation analyses across multiple benchmarks, including extensive Appendix C results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds embedding visualizations and classifier-count stability results in Figure 5 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The underlying ID/OOD correlation audit, classifier training approaches, and ColoredMNIST generation algorithm remain unchanged. The new embedding and stability analyses supplement evaluation without introducing a new training or inference method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian/mixture simulations, ColoredMNIST variations, and nine benchmark families in Appendix C. The new UMAP analyses use existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated domain-general/domain-specific logistic regressions, vision backbones, and BERT/DistilBERT families are retained. Added discussion of other algorithms and CLIP does not introduce a new reported comparator experiment.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the well-specification threshold from R < 0.5 to R < 0.3. Appendix B, Equation 38, removes the simulation generator's random-flip factors; this is a reported setting revision without evidence that the retained plots were rerun. Figure 5 introduces fitting UMAP on held-out ID examples and applying it to OOD examples.

E4.justification: v3 adds UMAP case studies examining spurious-feature versus class clustering in ColoredMNIST, Waterbirds, SpawriousO2O Hard, and PACS (Figure 5). It also adds classifier-count sensitivity analysis (Table 3), substantially expanding the mechanism and reliability checks.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained regression p-values and standard errors, v3 adds a bootstrap procedure with 1,000 resamplings and a 95% confidence criterion for establishing classifier-count convergence across benchmark splits (Table 3). It also newly specifies random-seed variation, without establishing an increase in training runs relative to v2.

E6.justification: v3 adds embedding findings and convergence-count results, while retaining the existing Appendix C correlation-table values. Table 1 changes SpawriousM2M Hard Env 0 from slope 0.16 and R = 0.29 to slope 0.76 and R = 0.94, marking it misspecified. However, v3 Table 13 retains the original Env 0 values and assigns the replacement values to Env 1.

T1.justification: v2's Gaussian, linear-shift Corollary 1 is replaced by Theorem 2 claiming necessary-and-sufficient conditions under symmetry, nonlinear shifts, and conditional independence, supported by a new monotonicity lemma and proof. Definition 2 changes its quantifier from all distribution pairs to existence of a pair. The finite-mixture proof in Appendix A.8 is removed, with the underlying assertion retained through citation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions foreground necessary-and-sufficient characterization in v3, extending beyond v2's headline sufficient conditions and Gaussian-only appendix corollary. The contribution list also adds a visualization tool. The central claim that many benchmarks inadequately test robustness to spurious correlations remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds embedding-based mechanism explanations and explicit binary-classification, symmetry, and conditional-independence limitations. Its discussion shifts from an inconclusive assessment of existing algorithms to highlighting published advantages over ERM on well-specified benchmarks. It also adds dataset-availability selection-bias arguments and removes the extended causal-benchmarking discussion in Appendix D.

D1.justification: v3 newly reports classifier-pool sizes by split, clarifies using pretrained language embeddings with lower-capacity downstream classifiers, and adds a visualization-tool link. The existing architecture specifications, augmentation details, and hyperparameter ranges remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 expands positioning through a worst-case stress-testing discussion comparing conventional transfer evaluation with ImageNot, and connects the conclusion to broader evaluation-validity research. It adds relevant methodological references and removes substantial causal-representation literature associated with Appendix D, while retaining a shorter discussion of that connection.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, theoretical explanations, discussion, and conclusion are rewritten. v3 introduces Preliminaries/Main Results subdivisions, moves benchmark descriptions into related work, separates applications from downstream implications, and broadly replaces model/predictor terminology with classifier.

P2.justification: v3 adds the cow/camel schematic, four-panel UMAP figure, and classifier-count table; redesigns Table 1; and changes typography, title/author layout, headers, and figure/table placement throughout. The overview figure replaces its Waterbirds panel with an existing CivilComments result; both underlying results remain in the appendices.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful bootstrap stability checks, embedding analyses, and clearer applicability limits. However, its expanded Theorem 2 applies Lemma 2 without establishing the shared score-distribution assumptions needed for that comparison, and Table 1 introduces a benchmark classification inconsistent with Appendix C.3.4. These issues affect central claims and recommendations, making the net quality change uncertain.
